name: hdie_svc_vm_kshare_r6b
hold_budget_reason: CDC leaf (hbm/stream async_gray_fifo profile: cmd/wcmd/fill Gray FIFOs + fault_cdc)
slot_change_request: SVC-SMALL 10-18 (from HBMA-SVC 10-17): d4g GEN0 binds ot_hbm_svc_vm_kshare #(.MUT(0),.KRL1(1)) x16 (vmks_SW0..7, vmks_NW0..7; SYNTH, no slot in grants_d4g). 7,340 port bits cannot sit on the d4f 146.88 x 146.88 slot (12.5 pins/um); pin-derived outline 432 x 388.8 (10 x 9 lattice cells): E svg K request 1,380 b (3.5/um), S controller K 2,488 b (5.8/um), N svg K response + VM/WB command + fills 2,319 b (5.4/um), W WB K port 1,156 b (3.0/um). Top = ot_hbm_svc_vm_kshare_splitstrap #(.KRL1(1)) (byte-identical to ot_hbm_svc_vm_kshare except strap sm -> sm_stream + sm_hbm, both tied to the same SM index): die.v rebind needed (H-D4G: cell + 2 strap pins); vmks_NW* placed MX (controllers north of the NW band). r6 (STEWARD-HBMd/PINREG-KS 10-23): outline 540.0 x 367.2 (FB), same faces; pin-bound (r5a 432 x 388.8 has 1,642 um perimeter for 7,343 pins) -> die slot update with the HBMd chain.

reset_landing.reason: the RTL lands it: stream_rst_n -> srst_q (stream_clk), hbm_rst_n -> hrst_q (hbm_clk), one flop per domain at entry, so each reset port has one sink and core fan-out starts at a register; the kit landing has one clock and cannot land two async domains (ROOT-HBM 10-19)

pin_regs.reason: PINREG=1 (STEWARD-HBMd/PINREG-KS 10-23, r6): the RTL registers every pin itself -- every data/valid INPUT (g_k_*, w_k_*, c_kr_*, c_k_wr_done) lands in ONE plain flop (pin -> flop D, no gate; data free-running, valid async-cleared), every OUTPUT leaves a flop (skid / ring head, rdy flops, wr_done / fill / fault flops); io_flop_at_pins anchors them FIRM at their faces. Named exception: ready inputs c_k_rdy / g_kr_rdy (8 pins) stay direct (registering them changes the controller / svg protocol), reset pins land on one async-clear flop per domain. A kit pin stage cannot span the two async_gray_fifo domains and would add unpriced K-port latency.

job.purpose: kshare r6b (FB; STEWARD-HBMd/PINREG 01:40 PLAN, coordinator tile review 10-23: r5a blob far from the S pins, 3,647 inputs entering skid D-muxes): r5a + PINREG=1 -- every data/valid input pin lands in ONE plain flop anchored FIRM at its face (io_flop_at_pins cols 6), group / WB skids -> 3-entry rings with registered rdy, KRL1 response ring 3 -> 4, c_k_wr_done pin flop; +1 hbm edge on group req / WB write / response / VM beat / wr_done (COORD-REVIEW-QUEUE sign-off); ready inputs c_k_rdy / g_kr_rdy direct (named exception). Outline 540.0 x 367.2, faces as r5a (E svg, S controllers, N long-haul, W WB). Proof: PINREG 0 vs 1 lockstep (results/rtl/hbmd_pinreg_ks_r6_1023).

safe_design_checklist.1_pins: PINREG=1: every data/valid input lands on one plain face flop (pin -> D, no gate), every output already leaves a flop; exception 8 ready inputs (c_k_rdy, g_kr_rdy: controller / svg protocol, coordinator sign-off) + 2 reset pins (async-clear landing). io_flop_at_pins cols 6 (S face 2,484 face flops > 4 x 560). <= 4.6 pins/um every face.
safe_design_checklist.2_reach: max face-to-face lane path E -> S ~600 um split by pin flop -> ring -> B skid head flop -> pin; each hop <= ~300 um at 833/1024 ps. Gate measures.
safe_design_checklist.3_fanout: rings / skids keep the r5a slicing (12-bit ring slices with kept wp/rp, kept slice ANDs; new A/E rings 29/24 slices take in_v/pop through 2 kept group ANDs); pin flops load the ring entries (3/4 loads). Native census in gate.
safe_design_checklist.4_depth: unchanged logic; the pin -> head/tail D-mux IO path becomes pin -> flop; ring read = 3:1 / 4:1 mux on rp before the B select (was the skid head flop).
safe_design_checklist.5_storage: no macros; A/E 3-entry rings, C 4-entry ring (KRL1), sliced.
safe_design_checklist.6_floorplan: enlarged to the pin-legal perimeter (7,343 pins need >= 1,836 um at 4/um; r5a 1,642): never squeezed; fill ~10% is the pin-bound consequence; lanes 0..3 in order along each face. Gate PNG decides.
safe_design_checklist.7_clock: two roots (stream, hbm) as r5a; span grows to the outline; gate --cts measures pin-flop spread <= 80 ps TT/FF.
safe_design_checklist.8_schedule: static; +1 hbm edge (recorded, COORD-REVIEW-QUEUE): group request -> controller, WB write -> controller, controller response -> group, controller VM beat -> fill CDC, c_k_wr_done -> g/w_k_wr_done; stream pins unchanged; II=1 kept (lockstep stream phase). r5a 2-level kept reset leaves unchanged; new pin valid flops on new leaves from hr1[4l+1] (unused by r5a), <= 32 loads.
